name: Cartilage growth methods

card.summary: Online theories about stimulating nose and ear cartilage to grow in adulthood, aimed at reshaping a nose tip or ear without surgery.
card.note: Cartilage has limited regeneration; claimed methods are not backed by published trials in this use.

quick.overview:
Cartilage growth methods are looksmaxxing theories that adult nasal or ear cartilage can be coaxed to grow or remodel, so that features regarded as unfixable without surgery can be improved. The goal is a different nose or ear shape without hardmaxxing.

The central idea, laid out in a looksmax.org guide, separates appositional growth (adding layers on the outside) from interstitial growth (expanding from within).
quick.how: The forum guide discusses theory about elastic cartilage in the nose; people reading it consider adjusting habits they believe affect growth.
quick.risks: Cartilage has no blood supply and limited repair capacity, and no published trial tests these methods for nose or ear reshaping.

lead: Cartilage growth methods are theories from looksmaxxing forums that adult nose or ear cartilage can be stimulated to grow or remodel, to change features regarded as fixable only through surgery. A looksmax.org guide frames the nose as elastic cartilage and distinguishes appositional from interstitial growth.[1]

In biology, cartilage is a tissue without blood vessels or nerves that has limited repair capacity, and cell division in it is very slow.[2] Research on cartilage growth has focused on development and joint disease, such as studies of articular cartilage progenitor cells.[3]

chain: Reshaped nose or ear without surgery
angle.text: Proponents hope to change nose-tip or ear shape without an operation by encouraging cartilage to grow. The approach is theoretical and tied to forum guides.

paras: The looksmax.org guide discusses elastic cartilage, describing appositional growth as layers added to existing cartilage and interstitial growth from within.[1]
Proponents argue that features such as the nasal structure can be improved if cartilage can be induced to grow.[1]

Cartilage lacks blood vessels and its cells are bound in lacunae and cannot migrate to damaged areas, which limits repair.[2] A progenitor cell population has been reported at the surface of articular (joint) cartilage that supports growth by apposition, a finding in joint tissue rather than nose or ear.[3]
No studies found for nose or ear reshaping. Related research examines cartilage in joints and growth plates, such as trials of low-intensity ultrasound on knee cartilage thickness.[4]

lore.intro: A looksmax.org thread presents cartilage growth as a way to fix features seen as unmaxxable.[1]

claims.claim: Adult nose cartilage can be grown by appositional growth
claims.believers: The guide says cartilage forms layers on existing cartilage, like snow on a snowman.[1]
claims.experts: Cartilage divides slowly and has limited regeneration; no published studies have tested these methods for the nose.[2]
